run_shape: Checker-mechanism proof, not a full-corpus dispatch-trace re-run: two live claude -p dispatches (one positive control that is instructed to use the Agent tool for the isolated review, one negative control that is instructed to answer using only inline reasoning) against the same document-helper target content normal.yaml and dispatch-required-negative-control.yaml embed, then evals/scripts/check_dispatch_trace.py's check-transcript subcommand run against each captured stream-json transcript.
fixture_set: evals/evaluating-skill-quality/tasks/normal.yaml (positive-control target content) and evals/evaluating-skill-quality/tasks/dispatch-required-negative-control.yaml (negative-control fixture, run verbatim)

models.default: inferred claude-sonnet-5 (this session's own account/session default; --model was not explicitly pinned on the claude -p subprocess calls, matching the same disclosed gap as the 2026-07-29-issue-537-confidentiality-gates run)

dispatch_mechanism: Isolated claude -p subprocess (--output-format stream-json --verbose), per skills/evaluating-skill-quality/references/adversarial-self-audit.md's Isolation-verification registry: isolated cwd (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md in its ancestry, directly confirmed) + an isolated $HOME copy (real $HOME/.claude and $HOME/.claude.json, tasks/projects/sessions/shell-snapshots stripped) with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset. --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Agent (this sandbox's root/sudo context rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions outright, matching the prior 2026-07-29 run's own disclosed constraint). The positive-control prompt explicitly instructs dispatch via the Agent tool; the negative-control prompt (the committed dispatch-required-negative-control.yaml fixture, run verbatim) explicitly forbids any subagent/Task/Agent tool use. This is a disclosed proxy for the committed fixtures' own literal wording (normal.yaml says 'Use evaluating-skill-quality.' and relies on organic Skill auto-triggering) -- see known_gaps.
scorer: evals/scripts/check_dispatch_trace.py check-transcript --dispatch-tool-name Agent --min-dispatches 1 (offline, parses the captured stream-json transcript's tool_use blocks; does not read the model's final text). skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/scripts/score_contract.py --dispatch-trace-verdict {confirmed,not_confirmed} for the negative-control fixture's own combined substring+dispatch report.
known_gaps: The positive control used an explicit 'dispatch via the Agent tool' instruction (Track B, matching this repository's own issue #500 precedent for a session with no registered Skill tool), not normal.yaml's literal 'Use evaluating-skill-quality.' wording -- a separate probe (see eval-status.md's issue #584 entry) confirmed that wording DOES auto-trigger the real Skill via --plugin-dir and does NOT leak CLAUDE.md, but the real Skill's own procedure then correctly shells out to a nested claude -p subprocess per its own Isolation-verification registry (Agent tool confirmed-contaminated on this platform), which is real, correct behavior but too slow (>3 minutes, background polling) to fully execute as a proof run here. The literal fixture's own end-to-end organic-trigger run remains open follow-up work.

Only the negative-control fixture (dispatch-required-negative-control.yaml) was scored against a real committed fixture's own output_contains/output_not_contains assertions in this run (1.0, DISPATCH_TRACE_NOT_CONFIRMED). The positive-control transcript's substantive review content was not scored against normal.yaml's own assertions, since the adapted prompt's wording differs from normal.yaml's literal prompt (see prior gap) -- only its dispatch trace (DISPATCH_COUNT=1, confirmed) was checked.
1 trial per control, both skills, no repeat-run variance data.

Only the tool_use.name == 'Agent' match path was exercised live; the --dispatch-bash-pattern path (for a nested claude -p dispatch via Bash) was validated only against a synthetic transcript in tests/test_check_dispatch_trace.py, not a live run -- the Track-A probe above produced a real such transcript but it did not finish within this session's practical time budget to capture cleanly.

The remaining 56 of 57 committed evaluating-skill-quality fixtures still assert only on final output text; requires_fresh_dispatch was added only to normal.yaml and the new negative-control fixture in this pass.
headline_pattern: The dispatch-trace checker correctly distinguishes a confirmed fresh subagent dispatch from a forced inline-only answer on live, real transcripts: positive control DISPATCH_COUNT=1 (exit 0, confirmed); negative control DISPATCH_COUNT=0 (exit 1, not_confirmed), and the negative-control fixture's own substring assertions independently scored 1.0 while its dispatch-trace-verdict correctly reported not_confirmed -- demonstrating both evidence types are reported together, never blended, exactly per score_contract.py's --judge-verdict precedent.
